summary: Axel Klein is a scholar of Japanology. He studied at the University of Bonn (1987–1994), where he was a wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter (1998–2007), later holding posts at the German Institute for Japanese Studies (2007–2011) and the University of Duisburg-Essen (2012).

Axel Michaels works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg, under Laxmi Nath Shrestha, and at Kiel University. He served at the Nepal Research Centre, Kiel, University of Bern, and Heidelberg University.

Ayu Khandro was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. She studied under Nyala Pema Dündul, Chokgyur Lingpa, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, and Drodul Pawo Dorje, and taught A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé and Namkhai Norbu.

Ayya Khema was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. She studied under Laurence Khantipalo Mills, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, and Matara Sri Ñāṇarāma. She founded Wat Buddha Dhamma and Sakyadhita, and taught at Buddha-Haus from 1989.

B. Alan Wallace works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Amherst, Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt, and under several Tibetan teachers. He taught at Rabten Choeling, UC Santa Barbara, and founded the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies.

B. N. K. Sharma was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Madras, Presidency College Chennai, and under Satyadhyana Tirtha. He held posts at Annamalai University, Rajah's College, Poornaprajna Sanskrit College, and Ramnarain Ruia College.

B. R. Ambedkar was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Columbia, the London School of Economics, and University of London under John Dewey and Edwin Cannan. He later served at Sydenham College and Government Law College.

Baatr Kitinov is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. in World History from Moscow State University and serves as Associate Professor in the Department of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1935–1966), as Government Epigraphist, and as professor at Panjab University (~1965).
Baiei Henmi was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University and held a post at Tama Art University.

Baihui Wu was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1945–1951), served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University, and worked at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and its Institute of Philosophy (~1978).

Baij Nath Puri was an Indologist and historian. He earned his M. Lit. and D.Phil. from the University of Oxford (~1949–1951). He later served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1971–1976).

Bal Gangadhar Tilak was a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at Deccan College, Elphinstone College, and Government Law College, Mumbai. He co-founded the Deccan Education Society and taught mathematics at the New English School and Fergusson College.

Bal Krishen Thapar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University of the Punjab, Heidelberg University, and under Mortimer Wheeler. He was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981) and later chaired CCRT.
Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist. He held posts at Panjab University, where he served as an Assistant (attested 1932) and in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1941).

Bangwei Wang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Peking University (~1983–1987), where he became Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies around 1993.

Banikanta Kakati was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He served as a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and later as Dean and department head at Gauhati University (1948).

Bapudeva Sastri was a scholar of Indology. He studied at Sehore High School under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundiraja Misra, and Sevarama, and later taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

Barbara E. Ward was a Sinologist and anthropologist. She studied at Newnham College, University of London, and the LSE. She held posts at the University of London, Cambridge, CUHK (1978–1982), and headed the International Institute for Environment and Development (1973).

Barbara Gerke is a Tibetologist who earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held research posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (2011–2015), CSDS, and the University of Oxford (attested 2017).
